origins.section: Any Nonnegative Prices on the Budget Rows Give an Upper Bound
A Relaxed Plan Repaired Into a Feasible One Gives the Lower Bound
When the Pieces' Own LP Has Whole-Number Answers, the Best Bound Is the LP Bound

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-sign: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-sign: "The sign of λ matters: a negative price would reward overspending and break the first step." The bound holds only "for every λ ≥ 0", so the 2029 price of -0.2 is the error.
recorded.prompt:q-two-bounds: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-two-bounds: The Lagrangian value is an upper bound: "no plan is worth more than 26,642.5". "Every repaired plan is feasible, so its NPV is a lower bound z ≤ z*". So the optimum is at most 51,200, and their feasible 49,000 plan is within 2,200 of it.
recorded.prompt:q-integral: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-integral: "If the relaxed problem ... has an LP relaxation whose optimum is always a 0/1 plan, its integrality property, ... the best Lagrangian bound equals the LP bound: z_LD = z_LP. Each group here is a choice of at most one start among a handful, which is such a problem."

recorded.prompt:q-sign:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-sign:a: The page says prices may differ by year: "prices that differ by year do better still". Its example vector 'lam 0.6, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5, 0.3' still gives a valid bound, 27,226, which is above 24,260.
recorded.prompt:q-sign:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-sign:b: "L(λ) is an upper bound on z* for every λ ≥ 0". On the page, 'lam 1.0 everywhere' gives 37,284 'above the optimum by 13,024.0'. A high price only loosens the bound and never pushes it below the optimum.
recorded.prompt:q-sign:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-sign:d: Nothing on the page requires the prices to add up to 1. Its examples 'lam 0.3 everywhere' (sum 1.5) and 'lam 0.6, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5, 0.3' are all valid bounds above the 24,260 optimum.
recorded.prompt:q-two-bounds:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-two-bounds:a: "its NPV is a lower bound z ≤ z*". The repaired plan is only a lower bound; in the page's run it is "the plan $891k below" the optimum. A feasible plan worth 49,000 also shows the optimum is at least 49,000.
recorded.prompt:q-two-bounds:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-two-bounds:c: The Lagrangian bound is an upper bound and is not the optimum: "the Lagrangian bound $2,382.5k above it".
recorded.prompt:q-two-bounds:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-two-bounds:d: The repaired plan is only one feasible plan, a lower bound ("Every repaired plan is feasible, so its NPV is a lower bound"). Beating it does not mean the planners' plan breaks a row, and the stem says that plan meets every rule.
recorded.prompt:q-integral:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-integral:a: "That is a theorem, not an accident of the step rule."
recorded.prompt:q-integral:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-integral:b: Repaired plans give the lower bound and do not set L(λ). The page says the stall at the LP value "is a theorem, not an accident": z_LD = z_LP.
recorded.prompt:q-integral:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-integral:c: The update rule keeps prices at or above zero: "lam = {y: max(0.0, lam[y] - step * g[y]) ...}" and "never below zero".
